paper.title: The FNV Non-Cryptographic Hash Algorithm (draft-eastlake-fnv-21)
paper.venue: IETF Internet-Draft, 7 January 2024 (the FNV hash itself dates from 1991)

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm description in the draft: one generic n-bit FNV implementation with multi-limb arithmetic and the prime applied as shifts and adds; no code from the draft or other third parties copied. The two tables are included as hex strings in fnv_tables.inc (data only)
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: FNV-1a 32-bit and 64-bit of "", "a" and "foobar" match the 12 values of draft Appendix C (Table 3 without and Table 4 with a terminating zero byte)
the six FNV primes (32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024 bits) built from the stated form 2^s + 2^8 + b equal the hex values in Table 1

the six offset_basis values of Table 2 (32 to 1024 bits) are reproduced as the draft defines them, the n-bit FNV-0 hash of the 32 octets "chongo <Landon Curt Noll> /\../\" (the 1024-bit case exercises 32-limb arithmetic)

expected_values_source.what: Appendix C (test vectors), Table 1 (FNV primes) and Table 2 (FNV offset_basis values), and the definition of the offset_basis in section 2.2 of the draft
expected_values_source.note: the values are data copied from the draft (Table 1 and 2 by a script that checked each length). The draft prints the 64-bit value for "foobar" with a stray space as 0x85944171f 73967e8, which is the 16 digits 85944171f73967e8

negative_control: built with FNV_B_ADJ=1 (low-byte term of the 32-bit prime 0x93 changed to 0x94), the 32-bit prime prints 01000194 instead of 01000193, the 32-bit offset_basis becomes 5c738010 instead of 811c9dc5, the program prints FAIL and exits 1
not_checked: FNV-1 (multiply then xor) outputs and FNV-1a outputs for 128, 256, 512 and 1024 bits: the draft prints no test vectors for them (FNV-0 is exercised through the offset_basis check)
the draft's reference C code and its test driver, endianness conventions and XOR folding
hash quality, dispersion or collision claims, and speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about real hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, reproduces the 24 numbers printed in the draft (12 test vectors, 6 primes, 6 offset_basis values derived by the draft's own definition). It does not show any quality claim about FNV.
